sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: AWS operates infrastructure around the world. You need to understand how Regions, Availability Zones, and edge locations relate and when multi-AZ or multi-Region designs fit a requirement.
sections.callout: Where should the AWS workload run?

sections.title: Maestro Mental Model
bullets: AVAILABILITY ZONE → Isolated location within a Region
sections.callout: REGION = WHERE · AZ = ISOLATION · EDGE = CLOSER

sections.title: AWS Regions
paragraphs: An AWS Region is a distinct geographic area containing multiple isolated Availability Zones. Organizations select Regions based on user location, latency, regulations, data sovereignty, service availability, and recovery strategy.

sections.title: Availability Zones
paragraphs: Availability Zones are distinct, isolated locations within a Region. They are designed with independent infrastructure so a failure affecting one location is less likely to affect another, while low-latency connectivity supports resilient architectures.
sections.callout: Isolated location inside a Region → Availability Zone

sections.title: High Availability and Multiple AZs
paragraphs: High availability means designing systems to remain accessible when components fail. Distributing redundant resources across multiple Availability Zones helps a workload survive disruption in one AZ without losing the whole application.
sections.callout: High availability within one Region → Multiple Availability Zones

sections.title: Multiple Regions
paragraphs: Some organizations deploy resources in more than one AWS Region to meet geographic resilience, user-experience, or legal requirements.
bullets: Lower latency for geographically distant users
sections.callout: Geographically separate recovery or requirements → Multiple Regions

sections.title: Data Sovereignty
paragraphs: Data sovereignty concerns legal or regulatory requirements governing where data is stored or processed. These obligations can determine which Region an organization selects.
sections.callout: Geographic law or residency requirement → Region selection

sections.title: Edge Locations
paragraphs: Edge locations are points of presence used by supported AWS services to place content or networking capabilities closer to end users, improving delivery performance and reducing latency.
sections.callout: Deliver supported content closer to users → Edge location

sections.title: Amazon CloudFront
paragraphs: Amazon CloudFront is AWS's content delivery network (CDN). It can cache and deliver content through edge locations closer to users instead of sending every request to the application's origin.
sections.callout: CDN and edge delivery → Amazon CloudFront

sections.title: Edge and Infrastructure Extension Services

entries.title: AWS Local Zones
paragraphs: Place selected AWS services closer to large population and industry centers for applications that require very low latency.
entries.memoryHook: AWS services closer to a metro area.

entries.title: AWS Wavelength
paragraphs: Embeds selected AWS services within telecommunications providers' 5G networks for applications that need ultra-low latency to mobile devices.

entries.title: AWS Global Accelerator
paragraphs: Uses the AWS global network and static anycast IP addresses to route users to healthy application endpoints with improved availability and performance.
entries.memoryHook: Accelerate dynamic application traffic to healthy endpoints.

sections.callout: METRO PROXIMITY → LOCAL ZONES · 5G EDGE → WAVELENGTH · GLOBAL APPLICATION ROUTING → GLOBAL ACCELERATOR

table.caption: Separate the three global-infrastructure layers
rows: Point of presence closer to users

sections.title: GSA Scenario Recognition
bullets: Choose a geographic AWS location → Region
Remain available if one isolated location fails → Multiple AZs
Recover in a geographically separate AWS area → Multiple Regions
Deliver cached content globally with lower latency → Edge locations or CloudFront
Place selected services closer to a metro area → Local Zones
Run selected workloads at the 5G edge → Wavelength
Route dynamic application traffic over the AWS global network → Global Accelerator
Keep data in an approved jurisdiction → Region selection and data sovereignty
sections.callout: Location, resilience, proximity, or legal geography reveal the answer.

entries.title: Region vs. Availability Zone
paragraphs: A Region is a geographic area. An AZ is an isolated location within a Region.

entries.title: Multi-AZ vs. Multi-Region
paragraphs: High availability inside one Region → Multi-AZ. Geographic recovery, reach, or legal requirements → Multi-Region.

entries.title: Region vs. Edge
paragraphs: A Region hosts workloads and services. An edge location brings supported delivery capabilities closer to users.

entries.title: Latency Clue
paragraphs: Choose a nearby Region for workload placement; use edge services such as CloudFront for content delivery closer to users.
